- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The post-World War II era saw Japan facing many economic challenges, leading to various economic policies to develop the economy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Economic Stabilization Board (ESB) was established to supervise economic rehabilitation measures, regulating prices, wages, and profits.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In 1947, Japan implemented the Progressive Tax Law, which reduced the burden on the poor and redistributed wealth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Japanese government supported strategic industries through subsidies and priority access to resources, investing heavily in infrastructure and technology transfer.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The government invested in education and training to enhance workforce productivity and competitiveness.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Japan adopted a fixed exchange rate system with the US dollar in the early post-war period, later allowing the yen to float freely in the late 1970s.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Japan pursued an open trade policy, joining the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in 1955 and entering bilateral trade agreements.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The government created a stable financial system to improve access to credit and reduce interest rates, establishing the Bank of Japan (BOJ) as the central bank.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 1980s, Japan implemented deregulatory policies that eased regulations on industry and finance, increasing competitiveness and innovation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Japan undertook privatization and liberalization policies in the late 1980s and 1990s, opening industries like telecommunications and transportation to private investment.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Japan's economic policies contributed to making it one of the world's strongest economies.
